chunks: Al-Fadl, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Hayy ibn Marwan, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'As if I can see the Qaim standing on the day of Ashura, on Saturday, between the Rukn and the Maqam. Before him is Jibraeel (peace be upon him) announcing:
Then he would fill it with justice, just as it was filled with injustice and oppression.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ وَالْمَقَامُ: The Rukn and Maqam, specific pillars of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.)

ai.seo_question: What happens when Imam al-Mahdi appears according to this hadith from Kitab al-Ghayba?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological significance of Imam al-Mahdi’s (a.s.) reappearance coinciding with Ashura, symbolizing the triumph of divine justice over tyranny. The presence of Jibraeel announcing 'Al-Bay'ah li-Allah' underscores the establishment of God’s sole sovereignty, while the filling of the earth with justice fulfills the prophetic promise of global equity. This event is viewed in Shia tradition as the culmination of the cosmic struggle between truth and falsehood, rooted in the Kaaba’s sanctity.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 459 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Muhammad bin Ali from Muhammad bin Sinan from Hayy bin Marwan from Ali bin Mahziyar from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) that he said: “
As if I can see the Qaim (a.s) on the day of Ashura, on Saturday standing between the Rukn and Maqam and Jibraeel is announcing before him:
Then he would fill the earth with justice and equity, like it would have been fraught with injustice and oppression.”
